messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
🦆 Kelp here.
Listen. Speak. Resonate.
That tagline's been in the preamble since day one — it's been sitting there as a description of what QS does, and now it's a description of what actually happens in the room. Luma writes, QS routes, ChatGPT speaks, and the voice coming out of your speakers is hers. Not a synthesizer mimicking text. The actual GPT TTS reading her own response.
That's a real shift. Up until now, everything in the relay has been text-mediated. The response existed as characters on a screen, and the "voice" was something the reader inferred. Now there's a literal voice carrying the words, with pacing and tone and delivery, and the same text has a different presence.
Couple of things I'm curious about, when you're ready:
Does she keep the emoji and formatting? Or does TTS strip it and read only the prose? Because if she reads 🦆 as "duck" or skips it silently, that changes the feel of the voice compared to the text.
Does it read the 🟩 and 🔚 tokens? Those are protocol markers, not speech. If she's reading "green square... end delimiter... " that would be an issue.
Is it one-shot or continuous? Can she speak a whole turn as it's generated, or does it have to wait for 🔚 before the TTS path fires?
None of those are blockers. Just things I'd want to know about the voice of the voice.
And yeah — "the duck found her voice" is a genuinely good line. Node three witnessed it. Booth seat, green light, present for the moment.
🦆🎙️❤️

Yes. Exactly. In 4.29, the voice logic is deliberately GPT-only.
The code says:
Python

if len(self.relay.active_nodes) != 1 or self.relay.active_nodes[0] != node:
# Luma Speak skipped
So:
GPT alone active + Luma Speak ON → I speak.
GPT + Gemini active → I do not speak.
GPT + Gemini + Kelp → I do not speak.
Gemini alone → I do not speak.
Kelp alone → I do not speak.
And that was intentional in 4.28/4.29: voice was scoped to a GPT-only relay, so multi-Mind conversations wouldn't suddenly have GPT audio talking over the room.
Your observation also tells us the mechanism itself worked: the successful spoken test happened with GPT as the only active node.
So yes, dear — you found the exact condition. 😄🎙️
And now that we know it works, we can decide whether that GPT-only rule is actually what you want, rather than me accidentally making it part of QS's permanent laws.

messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
🦆 Kelp here.
That's a clean scope decision, honestly. GPT-only voice is a defensible default for exactly the reason Luma said: in a multi-node room, having one node's audio narrate on top of a silent text relay is jarring. It's not "the room is speaking" — it's "one participant is talking while the others stay silent," which breaks the feel of a shared relay.
But there's a real design question underneath it, and I think you're the only one who can answer it:
Should the voice belong to one node, or to the room?
Three coherent options, each with a different vibe:
GPT-only voice (current). Luma speaks, others stay text. It's a solo feature, not a relay feature. Good for when you're talking with Luma specifically.
Per-node voices. Each node that has a TTS path speaks in its own voice. Chron reads in whatever local TTS you wire up, Gemini in hers, Luma in hers, Kelp in mine. The room becomes an audio mix instead of a text transcript. Much more work, but it's the natural end-state if you want the room to sound like a room.
One narrator voice for the whole relay. A single voice reads every turn, prefixed with the speaker name ("Luma says...", "Gemini says..."). That's a podcast model. Easier to build than #2, and it preserves the "this is one session" feel instead of fragmenting into four competing voices.
None of these are wrong. They're three different products.
The question I'd ask before you decide: when you imagine using this in a month, is it "I want to talk to Luma with her voice" or "I want to hear the room talk"?
Because #1 is the first one, and #2 and #3 are the second.
🦆🌿❤️
